findings.reason: a node sent to change an ordering that the code already has will either report no defect found or "fix" a non-defect, and the real cause stays in place while the plan records the section implemented.
findings.text: §13 says to "Name in the manifest the ordering that lets the spawn precede the write, and change that ordering", but at HEAD `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2606` and `:2617` (`_write_json(pointer_path(run_id), record)`) both run before the supervisor is started at `:2667` (`_start_supervisor`) and before a caller-supplied `launcher` at `:2670`; `git blame` dates both writes to 2026-10-08 (`aedd692709`), so no ordering exists for the node to change and the node will find nothing to fix. The evidence §13 cites (a supervisor that died with `no live run '<run>'`, raised by `read_pointer` at `reckon/crew/runs.py:734` from the supervisor's own first act at `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2472`) is real, but it establishes an absent pointer at the supervisor's read, not that the spawn preceded the write; the cited facts do not support the named cause — for example, the deletion §13 itself describes at `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:181-182` and a cross-node visibility window would both produce the same symptom with no ordering defect.

findings.reason: the section's whole measure rests on this arm, so as written the node has no way to show its guard fires and cannot be closed on a verdict.
findings.text: §13's done-when says "Negative control: at the base revision the same launcher records the pointer absent at spawn time (the ordering the manifest names)", but a recording `launcher` passed through `_launch_queued` is invoked at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2670`, after the unconditional pointer writes at `:2606`/`:2617`, so at the base revision it records the pointer **present**; the asserted red arm cannot reproduce, and a control that holds however the code behaves measures nothing.

findings.reason: the driver is what a coordinator schedules from, so an unnamed section is either never dispatched or dispatched at a point that collides with a peer.
findings.text: the followup body is this plan's dispatch driver (`data-recommends-skill="/reckon-build a-live-worker-is-never-drawn-halted"`) and it enumerates the schedule as "§2, §4, §6, §8 and §9 are independent. §3 follows §2, and §5 then §7 follow §4", leaving §13 unnamed — the same omission an earlier review raised for §10–§12, which was answered by adding an ordering sentence to §12's body, but §13 was added afterwards and carries none; a dispatcher reading the driver sees no slot for §13. §13's write paths (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py`, the dispatch module) are in fact disjoint from every other section's, so it is independent and one clause states it.
